# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Implemented the remaining budget-remediation work in `tank_core`. Budget tracking now enforces a real end-of-tick closed-system guard on tracked nitrogen/carbon ticks by returning `SimError::BudgetImbalance` after invariants when a supposedly closed tick drifts. The shrimp lifecycle no longer creates mass in `system:daily_shrimp`: successful hatches and juvenile-to-adult growth now debit explicit dissolved N/C pools before adding new shrimp biomass, so reproducing closed systems stay conserved instead of silently minting biomass. I also documented the hourly chemistry DIC terms as an intentional open-system atmospheric-exchange shortcut, added a regression proving preset-like DIC rates break closed-system carbon conservation by design without tripping the guard, and expanded budget coverage with a reproducing-shrimp no-feed/no-export conservation test. The thermal reproduction fixture was rebalanced to keep that envelope test focused on reproduction under the new conserved-growth bookkeeping.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Audit the pending amendments against the current budget-ledger, shrimp lifecycle, chemistry DIC handling, and test fixtures to identify the remaining closed-system failure modes.
2. [Completed] Implement the runtime tracked-tick conservation guard and remediate `system:daily_shrimp` so hatching and juvenile maturation fund new biomass from explicit dissolved N/C pools instead of creating mass.
3. [Completed] Document the hourly DIC exchange shortcut as intentional open-system behavior and add regression coverage for preset-rate carbon drift plus reproducing-shrimp closed-system conservation.
4. [Completed] Rebalance the thermal reproduction fixture for the new conserved-growth model and run focused plus full-package validation to confirm the budget fixes did not regress broader `tank_core` behavior.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo test -p tank_core --test budget_tracking -- --nocapture` passed (14 tests, including the new reproducing-shrimp closed-system conservation regression and the preset-DIC open-system carbon regression).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test shrimp_population -- --nocapture` passed (8 tests).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test thermal_reproduction_penalty -- --nocapture` passed.
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test events -- --nocapture` passed (6 tests).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test water_change_mass_balance` passed (8 tests).
- `cargo test -p tank_core` passed across the full `tank_core` suite.
- `cargo clippy -p tank_core -- -D warnings` passed.

## Outstanding Risks

- Shrimp eggs are still implicit until hatch; mass is now conserved by debiting explicit dissolved pools on hatch and maturation, but a future phase may still want a first-class egg/clutch biomass pool for save-schema clarity and finer-grained tracing.
- The tick-level guard only fires on closed nitrogen/carbon ticks. Open-system ticks such as feed, water changes, shrimp add/remove, filter cleaning, and non-zero `system:chemistry` DIC exchange still rely on their explicit budget entries rather than a hard conservation assertion.
- Snapshot-derived gross budgets can still collapse same-component turnover inside complex stages until those systems emit fully explicit source/sink deltas; the new guard catches unexplained closed-tick drift, but it does not by itself expose every internal pathway.
